# iliad-037 — new renderings (6.116–231)

Rows in the form of the conventions table. Every row here is a choice this part makes that the table does not already fix; where a row departs from the Odyssey's English or from a table row, the last column says why.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἄντυξ ἣ πυμάτη … ἀσπίδος ὀμφαλοέσσης (6.118; ἄντυξ of a shield) | "the rim which ran outermost of the bossed shield" | "the outermost rim of his bossed shield" | "rail" (kept for the chariot's ἄντυξ, 5.262), "edge", "last rim"; πύματος "last, outermost"; ὀμφαλόεσσα keeps "bossed" (4.448) |
| μεμαῶτε (dual, 6.120) · ἰόντε (dual, 6.121) | "the two eager" · "advancing" | "both of them eager" · "advancing" | "both eager to fight" alone (loses the dual in `l`); the table's μεμαώς "eager" |
| τίς δὲ σύ ἐσσι φέριστε καταθνητῶν ἀνθρώπων; (6.123) | "And who are you, best of mortal men?" | "Who are you, then, best of mortal men?" | "best one", "noble sir" (turned down at the Odyssey's φέριστε); φέριστε keeps the Odyssey's "best of men" with the genitive of 6.123 added; καταθνητῶν ἀνθρώπων keeps "mortal men" (θνητοῖσιν, 19.593) |
| δολιχόσκιον ἔγχος (6.126) | "long-shadowed spear" | "long-shadowed spear" | the table's row (3.346), unchanged |
| δυστήνων … παῖδες (6.127) | "of wretched men the sons" | "the sons of wretched men" | "unlucky", "unhappy" (the Odyssey's `i` for δύστηνος in odyssey-015, which the table's "wretched" row overrides) |
| ἀντιόωσιν + dative (6.127) | "meet" | "meet" | "face", "oppose", "withstand" (reserved for μένω with an object); ἀντιάω "meet" |
| θεοῖσιν ἐπουρανίοισι(ν) (6.129, 6.131) | "the gods of heaven" | "the gods of heaven" | "heavenly gods" (δῖος is "heavenly"), "celestial", "gods above"; ἐπουράνιος keeps the Odyssey's "of heaven" (17.484), and Οὐρανίωνες (5.373) is told apart by the note |
| δὴν ἦν (6.131, 6.139–140) | "long was he" · "was he … long" | "lived long" · "lived long" | "survived", "was long-lived" (μακρόβιος); δήν "for long" with the imperfect of "be" is "lived long" |
| ἐρίζω + dative of gods (ὃς ῥα θεοῖσιν ἐπουρανίοισιν ἔριζεν, 6.131) | "quarrelled" | "quarrelled" | "vied with" (the Odyssey's rendering of ἐρίζω with the immortals, odyssey-024 and odyssey-035, where the contest is of skill), "rivalled", "contended"; the Iliad table keeps "quarrel" for strife, and Lycurgus's act is a fight, not a contest of skill |
| μαινομένοιο Διωνύσοιο (6.132) | "raging Dionysus" | "raging Dionysus" | "mad", "frenzied"; μαίνομαι keeps "rage" (5.185); the note says it is the god's frenzy |
| τιθήνας (6.132) | "nurses" | "nurses" | "attendants", "tending women" |
| ἠγάθεον Νυσήϊον (6.133) | "the holy Nyseion" | "the holy Nyseion" | "Nysa", "the Nysian hill" (the place is not known); ἠγάθεος keeps the Odyssey table's "holy" |
| θύσθλα (6.134; rare, traditional sense "sacred implements of the rites") | "the sacred implements" | "their sacred implements" (+ note: meaning not known) | "thyrsi" (names an object the Greek does not), "sacrificial gear", "offerings", "cult objects" |
| κατέχευαν (θύσθλα χαμαὶ κατέχευαν, 6.134; of objects) | "poured down" | "let … fall" | "poured out", "threw down"; κατά + χέω "pour down" (2.670) in `l`, with `i` saying what pouring down is for implements |
| βουπλήξ (6.135) | "ox-goad" | "ox-goad" | "ox-whip", "ox-striker", "cattle-prod"; βοῦς "ox" + πλήσσω "strike" |
| ἀνδροφόνοιο Λυκούργου (6.134) | "man-slaying Lycurgus" | "man-slaying Lycurgus" | the table's ἀνδροφόνος row (1.242), unchanged |
| δύσεθ’ ἁλὸς κατὰ κῦμα (6.136) | "went down into the wave of the sea" | "went down into the wave of the sea" | "dived", "plunged", "sank" (add speed or depth the Greek lacks); δύω "go down into" as in the table's ἀνεδύσετο "rose up out of" (1.496) |
| κόλπῳ (Θέτις δ’ ὑπεδέξατο κόλπῳ, 6.136; of a goddess's bosom) | "in her bosom" | "in her bosom" | "in the fold of her dress" (the Odyssey table's `i` for κόλπος, 15.469, where the word is a woman's dress-fold: a departure, with the reason: here a goddess takes a god into her embrace, and the note says the word also means "gulf"), "in her lap", "in her arms" |
| δειδιότα · κρατερὸς … τρόμος (6.137) | "terrified" · "strong trembling" | "terrified as he was" · "strong trembling" | "frightened" (kept for φοβηθείς in l, the participle two lines up; i has "in fear"), "shaking"; δείδω "fear", τρόμος "trembling" (5.862) |
| ὁμοκλῇ (ἀνδρὸς ὁμοκλῇ, 6.137; dative of ὁμοκλή) | "rebuke" | "shouted rebuke" | "threat", "threatening cry", "shout"; follows the Odyssey table's ὁμοκλή "rebukes" (17.189), with `i` adding "shouted" for the verb ὁμοκλάω "shout at" that the noun is built on |
| ὀδύσαντο (6.138) | "were angry" | "were angry" | "hated" (kept for ἀπήχθετο), "were wroth", "took offence"; follows odyssey-094 (ὀδύσσατο "were angry with him") |
| ἀπήχθετο πᾶσι θεοῖσιν (6.140, 6.200) | "was hateful" | "was hateful" | "became hateful", "was hated by", "incurred the hatred of" (the aorist is inceptive, and the note says so); follows iliad-020 (ἀπήχθετο "was hateful") |
| εἰ δέ τίς ἐσσι βροτῶν οἳ ἀρούρης καρπὸν ἔδουσιν (6.142) | "one of mortals who the fruit of the plough-land eat" | "one of the mortals who eat the fruit of the plough-land" | "bread-eaters", "eat the fruit of the earth", "eat the grain of the field"; ἄρουρα keeps "plough-land" (Odyssey table) |
| ἆσσον ἴθ’ (6.143) | "nearer come" | "come nearer" | "come on", "approach", "step up"; ἆσσον "nearer" as in the Odyssey's ἆσσον "nearer" (odyssey-043, -050) |
| ὀλέθρου πείραθα (6.143) | "the limits of destruction" | "the limits of destruction" | "the end", "the bounds", "the verge of death"; follows the Odyssey's "the limits of destruction" (odyssey-106) |
| γενεή (6.145, 6.150, 6.211: descent · 6.146, 6.149: a generation) | "lineage" · "generation" | "lineage" · "generation" | "race" (kept for γένος), "birth", "family" · "generations" in the plural (the Greek has the singular); one noun, two English words, and the note on 6.145 says so |
| ἐρεείνεις (6.145) | "ask" | "ask about" | "question" (kept for ἐρέεινε, 6.176, where the object is a person), "inquire into" |
| φύλλα … χέει / φύει / τηλεθόωσα (6.147–149) | "pours" · "puts forth" · "thriving" | "scatters" · "puts forth" · "thriving" | "flourishing" (shipped for τεθαλυῖα, per the Odyssey table), "luxuriant", "in leaf"; τηλεθόων keeps the Odyssey's "thriving" (τηλεθάων, 7.114) |
| ἔαρος … ὥρη (6.148) | "of spring the season" | "the season of spring" | "the hour", "the time"; ὥρη "season" as in the table's 2.468 row |
| κέρδιστος (6.153) | "the shrewdest" | "the shrewdest" | "the cunningest", "craftiest", "most gainful", "greediest" (cunning is reserved for μῆτις; "greedy" for κέρδος would mis-state it; the Odyssey table's κερδαλέος "shrewd and profit-seeking" and πολυκερδής "alert to every advantage" are the family; "most alert to advantage" is the sense and "shrewdest" the short form) |
| Αἰολίδης · Ἱππολόχοιο πάϊς (6.154, 6.119) | "Aeolus’-son" · "Hippolochus’ son" | "son of Aeolus" · "son of Hippolochus" | patronymic pattern of Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son" / "son of Atreus" |
| τέκεθ’ · τίκτεν · ἔτικτε (of fathers, 6.154, 6.155, 6.206) · ἔτεκε (of mothers, 6.196, 6.199) | "begot" · "bore" | "begot" · "bore" | "fathered", "sired" (turned down at 2.628); the table's τίκτω |
| ἠνορέη ἐρατεινή (6.156) | "lovely manliness" | "lovely manliness" | "desirable manhood", "lovely strength"; ἠνορέη keeps "manliness" (4.303, odyssey-119); ἐρατεινός keeps "lovely" |
| ὤπασαν (6.157) | "granted" | "granted" | "gave", "bestowed" (kept for δῶκε and for the Odyssey's ὀπάζων "bestowing"); follows odyssey-038 (ὤπασε "granted") |
| φέρτερος … Ἀργείων (6.158–159) | "stronger … than the Argives" | "stronger than the Argives" | "the best of the Argives" (the Odyssey's φέρτατος "by far the best" is the superlative), "better", "greater" |
| Ζεὺς … ὑπὸ σκήπτρῳ ἐδάμασσε (6.159) | "under the sceptre subdued" | "had made them subject to his sceptre" | "overcame" (kept for the victorious δαμάζω, 5.106), "tamed", "brought under"; the object (the Argives) is left out in the Greek and supplied in `i`; the table's δαμεῖεν "be made subject" (3.301) |
| ἐπεμήνατο (6.160) | "went mad" | "went mad with desire for him" | "was frantic for", "raved after", "lusted"; μαίνομαι keeps "rage / go mad" |
| κρυπταδίῃ φιλότητι μιγήμεναι (6.161) | "in secret love to be mingled" | "to lie with him in secret love" | "illicit love", "stolen love"; follows the Odyssey table's μίγη φιλότητι "was mingled in love" / "lay in love with" |
| ἀγαθὰ φρονέοντα (6.162) | "thinking good thoughts" | "who thought good thoughts" | "well-meaning", "right-minded", "honourable"; ἀγαθός "good" |
| ψευσαμένη (6.163) | "having lied" | "lying" | "falsely", "with a lie"; ψεύδομαι "speak falsely, lie" |
| τεθναίης … ἢ κάκτανε (6.164) | "May you be dead … or kill" | "May you die … or else kill" | "Die … or kill" (an imperative the Greek does not use); the perfect optative is a wish |
| οὐκ ἐθελούσῃ (6.165) | "me not wishing" | "when I did not wish it" | "unwilling", "against my will" (kept for ἀέκων, which is "unwilling"); ἐθέλω "wish" as in the Odyssey table (17.11) |
| χόλος λάβεν οἷον ἄκουσε (6.166) | "anger seized, at such a thing as he heard" | "anger seized the lord at what he heard" | "wrath" (μῆνις), "rage", "fury"; χόλος "anger" |
| ἄναξ (ἄνακτα, 6.166; Λυκίης ἄναξ, 6.173) | "the lord" · "the lord of wide Lycia" | "the lord" · "the lord of wide Lycia" | "king" (kept for βασιλεύς, 6.163), "master", "prince"; follows the table's ἄναξ "lord" |
| σεβάσσατο (6.167) | "felt awe" | "felt awe" | "scrupled", "was reverent", "revered", "shrank" (kept for ἀλέεινε); "awe" is reserved for the σέβας family |
| ἀλεείνω (ἀλέεινε 6.167, ἀλεείνων 6.202) | "avoided" · "avoiding" | "shunned" · "shunning" | "shrank from", "kept away from"; follows the table's κῆρ’ ἀλεείνων "death-fate avoiding" / "shunning death" (3.32) |
| σήματα λυγρά · σῆμα κακόν (6.168, 6.178) | "grievous signs" · "the evil sign" | "grievous signs" · "the evil sign" | "baneful tokens", "deadly signs", "marks"; σῆμα "sign", λυγρός "grievous", κακός "evil" |
| γράψας ἐν πίνακι πτυκτῷ (6.169) | "having scratched in a folded tablet" | "having inscribed … on a folded tablet" | "written" in `l` (γράφω "scratch", as in ἐπέγραψε "grazed", 4.139), "a folded writing-tablet", "a hinged board", "platters" (the Odyssey's πίνακες of meat, a different sense of the noun); πίναξ "tablet" here |
| θυμοφθόρα (6.169; sense not clear) | "heart-destroying" | "heart-destroying" (+ note: sense not clear) | "life-destroying", "deadly", "soul-corroding"; follows the Odyssey table's θυμοφθόρος (19.323, 10.363) |
| ᾧ πενθερῷ (6.170) · γαμβροῖο / γαμβροῦ (6.177, 6.178) | "his own father-in-law" · "his son-in-law" | "his own father-in-law" · "his son-in-law" | "his wife's father", "brother-in-law" (the Iliad's γαμβροῖσι at 5.474 is a different relation); ἑκυρός is the husband's father; γαμβρός "son-in-law" as in the Odyssey (odyssey-012, -019) |
| ὑπ’ ἀμύμονι πομπῇ (6.171) | "under the blameless escort" | "under the blameless escort" | "unfailing", "noble", "faultless" (each picks a sense of ἀμύμων); follows the Odyssey table's πομπή "escort" and ἀμύμων "blameless" |
| προφρονέως (6.173) | "readily" | "readily" | "willingly", "heartily", "with a ready heart"; follows iliad-034 (προφρονέως "readily") |
